newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower but trend remains bullish.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower but trend remains bullish.

text.p: French shares opened lower on profit-taking on Monday after Friday's slide on Wall Street from record highs but dealers said the trend remained bullish.

Technical analysts said there could be a short-term downward correction and if the blue-chip index fell below 2,600 the next support would be at 2,577. But if the market rose and broke resistance ay 2,631/32, it could rise to 2.650/52 and 2,6070/72.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 13.84 points or 0.53 percent at 2,613.58 at 0913 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,619 from 2,631 on Friday's close.

According to a poll conducted by the Sofres institute for the La Tribune newspaper, 55 percent of traders see a further rise in French shares in the coming weeks, 12 percent a fall while 32 percent expect a status quo.
Aluminium group Pechiney fell four percent to 246.10 francs after its 1996 sales fell by four percent and reiterated its warning of a loss of the second half.
Renault falls another 3.51 percent to 118.20 on its profit warning last week.
Michelin, down 1.5 percent at 336.40 francs, said it would convert early a convertivble bond issue.
